title: Test competing visual instructions
goal: Separate wording emphasis from model-specific prompt weighting syntax.
explanation: “Massive” and “tiny” describe relationships, but a generator may interpret them unpredictably. Numerical weighting syntax is provider-specific and may be ignored entirely. Start with plain language and inspect the image; do not claim a model used a weighting mechanism merely because you typed special punctuation.
sampleInput: Scene: a small kitten beside a large fictional dragon in a wide empty courtyard. Both subjects must be fully visible. Compare: dragon twice the kitten’s height; dragon ten times the kitten’s height; kitten larger than dragon.
prompt: Create one original illustration of the specified scene. Keep both subjects fully visible at the same distance from the camera. Change only their relative height: [chosen condition]. No text, logos, recognizable characters or extra animals.
workedExample: A test sheet measures the approximate visible height ratio and notes perspective or cropping. If the dragon is mostly off-frame, it does not demonstrate a controlled 10:1 size relationship. The result may be a failed condition, not an artistic success.

steps.title: Fix scene and framing
steps.text: Keep viewpoint, courtyard and subject count constant.

steps.title: Vary one relationship
steps.text: Generate the three plain-language size conditions and record model/settings.

steps.title: Measure visibly
steps.text: Estimate each subject’s height from the image and note perspective/cropping.

steps.title: Try one supported control
steps.text: Only if provider documentation describes weights, test that syntax separately from the language experiment.

steps.title: Report limits
steps.text: Retain failed images and distinguish observed results from assumptions about model internals.

checks: Both subjects are visible in each scored result, or cropping is explicitly recorded as a failure.
Only the size relationship changes in the primary prompt comparison.
Provider-specific weighting is not presented as universal or inferred from appearance alone.
commonMistakes: Treating arbitrary punctuation as a cross-provider weighting standard.
Confusing foreground perspective with actual relative size.
offline: Make three simple silhouette sketches and measure the height ratios manually.
reflection: How did perspective make the size comparison harder?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Both subjects are visible in each scored result, or cropping is explicitly recorded as a failure.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Only the size relationship changes in the primary prompt comparison.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Treating arbitrary punctuation as a cross-provider weighting standard.
